title: Bubble and Squeak
subtitle: British fried leftover potato and cabbage cakes
excerpt: Bubble and squeak is the classic British use of Sunday roast leftovers: mashed potato and cooked cabbage (or Brussels sprouts) mixed together and fried in butter until a golden crust forms on each side. The name comes from the sounds the vegetables make in the pan. It is simple, frugal, and one of the most satisfying ways to use leftover potato.
sourceNotes: Bubble and squeak has been mentioned in British cookbooks since the 18th century, where it originally referred to a dish of cold boiled beef fried with vegetables. By the 19th century, the beef had disappeared and only the potatoes and greens remained. Today it is the classic use for leftover roast vegetables, particularly common after Christmas when Brussels sprouts and roast potatoes are abundant.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Leftover potato and cabbage from the night before works perfectly.

content.text: Cold mashed potato from the fridge works best -- it holds its shape better than freshly made. The mixture should have roughly two parts potato to one part greens. Press the cake firmly into the pan and do not move it for 5 minutes -- the crust needs time to form. Flip only once.

items.prepNote: cooked and mashed (leftover mash is ideal)
cooked and roughly chopped (or leftover sprouts)

content.text: Melt half the {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Fry {{onion}} onion for 5 minutes until soft. Combine the onion with {{potatoes-floury}} potato, {{cabbage-savoy}} cabbage, {{salt-table}} salt, and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Mix well and form into one large flat cake, or individual patties.

Heat the remaining {{unsalted-butter}} butter and {{vegetable-oil}} oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Add the bubble and squeak cake(s). Press down firmly with a spatula. Cook without moving for 5 to 7 minutes until a deep golden crust forms underneath.
Flip carefully and cook for a further 5 minutes until golden on the second side. Serve immediately with fried or poached eggs, or as a side dish alongside cold roast meat.

items.symptom: The bubble and squeak falls apart when flipping
items.cause: The potato mixture was too loose, or the crust had not formed yet.
items.fix: Do not flip until you can see a brown crust starting to form around the edges when you lift a corner. If the mixture is very loose, add another spoonful of cold mashed potato to bind it. Work with individual patties rather than one large cake if it keeps breaking.

content.text: Bubble and squeak is a Monday dish -- the leftovers of Sunday's roast made into something new. It is made across Britain after Sunday roasts and especially on 26 December (Boxing Day) when the Christmas leftovers are transformed. The dish is eaten for breakfast, lunch, or as a side dish at any meal. It is one of the most enduring examples of the British tradition of waste-nothing cooking.
